changes.before: Labor market conditions have improved in recent months; the unemployment rate has declined but remains elevated.
changes.after: However, growth in employment has slowed in recent months, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.

changes.before: Household spending and business fixed investment have continued to advance.
changes.after: Household spending appears to be rising at a somewhat slower pace than earlier in the year.

changes.before: Inflation has picked up somewhat, mainly reflecting higher prices of crude oil and gasoline.
changes.after: Inflation has declined, mainly reflecting lower prices of crude oil and gasoline, and longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.

changes.before: Consequently, the Committee anticipates that the unemployment rate will decline gradually toward levels
changes.after: Consequently, the Committee anticipates that the unemployment rate will decline only slowly toward levels

changes.before: The Committee also decided to continue its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities as announced in September.
changes.after: The Committee also decided to continue through the end of the year its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities.
This continuation of the maturity extension program should put downward pressure on longer-term interest rates and help to make broader financial conditions more accommodative.

changes.before: The Committee will regularly review the size and composition of its securities holdings and is prepared to adjust those holdings as appropriate to promote a stronger economic recovery in a context of price stability.
changes.after: The Committee is prepared to take further action as appropriate to promote a stronger economic recovery and sustained improvement in labor market conditions in a context of price stability.

parsed.rationale: The Committee extended the maturity extension program through year-end, a new easing action, while downgrading its assessments of employment, spending and inflation. It also added an explicit readiness to take further action tied to labor market improvement.

spans.quote: Labor market conditions have improved in recent months; the unemployment rate has declined but remains elevated.
Household spending and business fixed investment have continued to advance.
Inflation has picked up somewhat, mainly reflecting higher prices of crude oil and gasoline.
Consequently, the Committee anticipates that the unemployment rate will decline gradually toward levels
The Committee also decided to continue its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities as announced in September.

The Committee will regularly review the size and composition of its securities holdings and is prepared to adjust those holdings as appropriate to promote a stronger economic recovery in a context of price stability.
However, growth in employment has slowed in recent months, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.
Household spending appears to be rising at a somewhat slower pace than earlier in the year.
Inflation has declined, mainly reflecting lower prices of crude oil and gasoline, and longer-term inflation expectations have remained stable.
Consequently, the Committee anticipates that the unemployment rate will decline only slowly toward levels
The Committee also decided to continue through the end of the year its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of securities.
This continuation of the maturity extension program should put downward pressure on longer-term interest rates and help to make broader financial conditions more accommodative.
The Committee is prepared to take further action as appropriate to promote a stronger economic recovery and sustained improvement in labor market conditions in a context of price stability.
